SECTION 2: TEACHING CONTENT

Hello Learner. Welcome to an English program for grade four. Today, we are going to learn how to use constructed forms of verbs, positive and negative statement s. Your radio teacher is Joyce Agik. Welcome to the program. - Hello learner. Welcome to the program. Learner, I want you to listen to these sentences. My name is Cow. I can eat grass. But I cannot eat meat. My name is Cow. I can eat grass. But I cannot eat meat. My name is Hen. I have wings, but I do not have horns. My name is Hen. I have wings, but I do not have horns. Learner. Tell me something you cannot eat. - Tell me something you do not have. - Did you say I cannot eat snakes? I do not have money?. Those are good sentences. Learner I want you to write the following sentences in your exercise book. Number one, my name is Goat. My name is not Sheep. My name is Goat. My name is not sheep. - We are dogs. We are not wild animals. We are dogs. We are not wild animals. - I have wings, but I do not have horns. I have wings, but I do not have horns. - I can eat grass, but I cannot eat meat. I can eat grass, but I cannot eat meat.

Learner, look at the sentences you have written. One. My name is Goat. It is positive. My name is not sheep. That sentence is negative. Number two. We are dogs. That is a positive sentence. We are not wild animals. That is a negative sentence. Number three. I have wings. That is positive. But I do not have horns. That is negative. And number four. I can eat grass. Positive. But I cannot eat meat. That one is negative. Learner, look at the sentences you have written and underline the words. Is not . are not . Do not and cannot. Look at the sentences you have written and underline the words. Is not . are not . Do not and cannot. The underlined wordss can be made shorter. For example, number one. Instead of is not we may say isn't . isn't Number two. Instead of are not, we may say aren’t . aren’t . Number three. Instead of do not, we may say don't . don't . And number four, instead of cannot, we may say can't. can't. Learner in the contracted verbs , the letter “O” is removed. And an apostrophe is added. in the contracted verbs , the letter “O” is removed. And an apostrophe is added. Now spell the word isn't. Isn't. - Spell the word isn't. Isn't. The spelling is. I. S. N apostrophe. T. Now spell the word aren’t. The spelling is. A. R. E. N. apostrophe. T. Spell the word don’t. The spelling is. D. O. N. apostrophe. T.

And now spell the word can’t. The spelling is. C. A. N. apostrophe. T. Very good, Learner. Now, write down the contracted forms of the following sentences. Write down the contracted forms of the following sentences. Number one. I cannot sleep today. I cannot sleep today. Number two. I do not have books. I do not have books. Number three. My name is not Paul. My name is not Paul. And number four. We are not happy. We are not happy. Learner, did you get the following answers? Number one, I cannot sleep today. The contracted form is. I can't sleep today. Number two, I do not have books. The contracted form is. I don't have books. Number three. My name is not Paul. The contracted form is. My name isn't Paul. And number four, we are not happy. The contracted form is. We aren't happy. Learner, you at home assignment. Form your own sentences using the contracted forms Don't, Can't, Isn't and Aren’t. Share with your parent, sibling or caregiver. Thank you, learner. In our lesson today, we have learned how to use contracted forms of verbs correctly. - That was an English program for grade four learners. SECTION 3: PRACTICE

1. Re-read the teaching content and underline three new words or ideas.
2. Explain the main idea of this topic to a parent or classmate in your own words.
3. Write five sentences using examples from your school or county.
4. Complete the revision quiz for this topic. Check answers only after finishing.

SECTION 4: CURRICULUM ALIGNMENT (KICD)

This lesson is aligned to the official KICD curriculum design for this sub-strand.

By the end of the Sub Strand,

the learner should be able to:

a) distinguish adverbs of

manner, time and place for

effective communication,

b) use adverbs of manner,

time and place correctly in

both oral and written

sentences,

c) realise the importance of

adverbs in oral and written

communication.

The learner is guided to:

• play games that involve grouping

adverbs of manner, time and

place,

• recite poems containing adverbs

of manner, time and place,

• construct sentences using

adverbs,

• listen to a story or poem read by

the teacher or from audio

recordings and respond to

questions,

• create word lists of adverbs and

use them to construct sentences

on a word processor or a web

page.

1. Where do you

live?

2. How do you do

your work?

3. When do we

come to school?
